title: Microframe emission probe and prefetch cache impact analysis
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Goal: Add a lightweight per-emission microframe probe that captures per-token timing slices and prefetch/KV-cache interactions so we can attribute latency and cost to token microframes (not just request-level). This ticket covers the instrumentation surface, trace/span naming, metric buckets, sampling strategy, downstream aggregation, and dashboarding/alerts.

Scope and success criteria:
- Emit a bounded-size event for each emission microframe containing: request_id, model_variant, emission_index, token_id (hashed), microframe_start_ms, microframe_end_ms, kv_prefetch_attempted:bool, kv_hit:bool, kv_latency_ms (if applicable), batch_size_at_emit, sequence_len_before_emit.
- Add corresponding OpenTelemetry span for microframe with parent request span and set attributes for kv_hit and batch_size. Span must be linkable to request-level trace and to subsequent token cache lookups.
- Produce three aggregated metrics: token_microframe_latency_{p50,p95,p99} per model_variant and per-tenant, kv_prefetch_rate, kv_hit_rate, and an economic metric tokens_cost_estimated which multiplies token work by model unit-cost.
- Ensure events are rate-limited and sampled (1% baseline, 10% for requests > 200ms or previously flagged anomalies).
- Wire events through existing metric/log pipeline (kinesis -> parquet -> materialized views) with schema versioning and a compact protobuf representation. Backfill not required.
- Dashboard: new token_microframe dashboard in Console with heatmap (emission_index vs latency), KV hit overlay, and a drilldown to traces. Add alert if p95 token_microframe_latency increases by >25% versus a 7-day baseline for a model_variant with >1000 tokens/day.

Telemetry schema notes:
- Metric names: rwin.token_microframe.latency_ms, rwin.token_microframe.kv_hit{0,1}, rwin.token_microframe.prefetch_attempt, rwin.token_microframe.cost_estimated.
- Histogram buckets: [0,1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512,1024] ms.
- Trace span naming: span.kind="emission", span.name="emission.microframe", attributes include emission.index, emission.token_hash, emission.kv_status, emission.batch_size, model.variant.

Operational considerations:
- Avoid logging raw tokens; token_id must be hashed (sha256 truncated) to protect PII and prevent sensitive content leakage.
- Payload size cap: events max 800 bytes. If an event would exceed the cap, switch to minimal envelope with pointer to sampled detailed view written to secure bucket.
- Rollout: feature flag behind "microframe_probe" with tenant opt-in. Start with internal tenants + top 5 customers.

Implementation plan:
1) Library changes: add MicroframeProbe interface in runtime-emitter (C++/Rust) with thin shim for OTel spans.
2) Server-side: emit protobuf event to telemetry topic; add schema in registry.
3) Pipeline: update parquet writer and materialized view to include microframe aggregates.
4) Console: dashboard panels + trace-link action.
5) Instrument CI smoke tests and synthetic load job to validate sampling and rate-limits.

Risks and tradeoffs:
- Sampling reduces resolution for low-traffic tenants; mitigate with adaptive sampling for anomalies.
- Additional TE telemetry cost; estimate +12% ingestion for sampled rollout.
- Hashing token ids prevents exact token-level debugging; we accept this for privacy.

Rollout milestones:
- Week 1: infra + proto schema, unit tests.
- Week 2: emitter lib + OTel span integration, internal tenant rollout.
- Week 3: pipeline aggregation, dashboard prototype.
- Week 4: customer opt-in and alert tuning.

Deliverables: implementation PRs, telemetry schema PR, Console dashboard PR, runbook entry, and cost estimate doc.
